ny_little_falls.blurb: Little Falls is a cluster of small crags around the town of Little Falls in the Mohawk Valley, just off the Thruway about 20 miles east of Utica. It is more of a local option than a destination. Top-roping is the most common style, followed by trad and a good amount of bouldering, with only a few sport routes. Moss Island is the main attraction, a small island in the Mohawk with a cliff 30 to 40 feet high along its south side and boulders on the north. Most routes there are best top-roped, and a few can be led on natural gear. The Dihedrals, downstream on the north bank, have routes that take good protection. Grades range from easy to 5.12, mostly 5.6 to 5.10.

pa_governor_stable.blurb: Governor Stable is a bouldering area on diabase, in a small wooded hollow near Elizabethtown in south central Pennsylvania. The hollow faces mostly south and is sheltered from wind, so on sunny days the boulders can feel 10 to 15 degrees warmer than the surroundings, which makes it a good cold-weather choice. Summer heat makes it harder going. The blocks are good quality and sit close together, so a lot of climbing fits in one day, and many landings are flat. Grades are spread across all levels: plenty of V0 to V4, a solid group at V5 to V7, and a few V8 to V10. Moby's and Friends, Pyramid Area, Warm-up Area and Breadloaf hold the most problems.

ab_bataan.blurb: Bataan is a sport crag above the Bow Valley near Canmore, with single-pitch routes of roughly 100 feet. Nearly everything is bolted, from 5.10 to 5.13, centred on 5.11 and 5.12, with a couple of 5.14s and a little bouldering. It is known for strong 5.11s. Sectors include Cloud Break, Eyes of Bataan, First Cave and The Cheese Grater. Expect a steep walk of about an hour or more on faint trails to reach the main walls. The crag can be climbed through the year, and the Eyes are the winter choice on clear, cold days, while spring runoff makes things wet and brings falling ice and rock, especially near the cave above The Slab.

_expect.name: Land of High Bouldering AKA The Ridge

az_land_of_high_bouldering_aka_the_ridge.blurb: The Ridge is a bouldering-only area just south of Flagstaff, part of the Lake Mary bouldering above Lower Lake Mary. The Drysdale Trail strings together about half a mile of walls with views of the lake and Mormon Mountain, and holds most of the problems. The Stone Cove is a compact set of walls with about two dozen clean lines from V0 to V4. Grades are mostly easy to moderate, with a big block from V0 to V4 and only a few V5 to V7. The Lake Mary bouldering as a whole sits on limestone bands and faces south, which makes it good in fall and spring and sometimes in winter.

ca_bmx_crags.blurb: BMX Crags is one of the larger sub-areas of Horsemen's Center in Apple Valley, in the High Desert at about 3,200 feet. The crags are scattered across a hillside. Sport routes are the main attraction, with a good number of boulder problems, some trad and a few top-ropes. Roped grades run mostly from 5.7 to 5.12, centred on 5.10 and 5.11, and boulders go from V0 to V5. Most crags face south or west and are often very sunny. Horsemen's Center as a whole is granite that resembles Joshua Tree's, and is a place to escape cold and wind in winter. Keepers Cove, BMX Area Bouldering, Black Corridor and Riders Ready Wall are the largest sectors.

ca_lake_george.blurb: Lake George is a granite climbing area in the Lakes Basin above Mammoth Lakes, in the Eastern Sierra at about 9,000 feet, with views down on the basin's lakes. Approaches take roughly 20 to 50 minutes. Sport is the most common style, followed by trad, with some alpine multi-pitch and a bit of bouldering. Most roped grades fall between 5.8 and 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 dominant. Horseshoe Piles and Dike Wall offer single-pitch sport climbing, while Crystal Crag mixes short sport routes with longer alpine climbs. Many crags face north, which helps on hot days, and a few face east. Across the Mammoth Lakes area the season runs from late April or May to November, depending on snow. Family Boulders add bouldering.
